title: Situation Brief — Know the Target
objective: Orient on actors, geography, and the commander's PIR before reporting begins.
storyText: You are the coalition intelligence cell supporting Gorgan leadership. Donovian rhetoric toward Gorgas has sharpened over the past two weeks, with renewed claims that Russian-speaking Zabzimekis are under threat. The commander wants you to integrate multi-domain reporting and warn of cross-border action.

studentTasks.prompt: In one sentence, restate the commander's PIR in your own words.

title: The Rumor Wave
objective: Identify the IO activity and its intended effect in the information environment.
storyText: Donovian state media and proxy social-media accounts simultaneously report that Gorgan nationalist militias are preparing attacks against Zabzimeki civilians. Reused footage and coordinated hashtags suggest a shaping campaign, not organic reporting.

studentTasks.prompt: Tag the activity. Select all that apply.
In 1–3 sentences, explain why this is disinformation rather than misinformation and identify the likely target audience.

title: Border Systems Go Dark
objective: Classify the actor and cyber kill-chain stage; distinguish cyber threat from cyber-enabled threat.
storyText: Gorgan CERT reports border CCTV blackouts, a credential-spray against a utility SCADA portal, ministry website defacement, and a spear-phish against a logistics contractor — all inside a 36-hour window. Infrastructure overlaps with a previously named Donovian-linked APT.

studentTasks.prompt: Best-fit threat actor category for this set of incidents:
What kill-chain stage best matches the spear-phish + credential spray?
Is this a cyber threat, a cyber-enabled threat, or both? Justify briefly.

title: Ground Picture Changes
objective: Pick the right GEOINT product for the gap and state imagery's limits.
storyText: EO imagery from D-3 shows ~40 tracked vehicles, fuel bowsers, and engineering bridging assets at a previously empty motor pool north of the border. D-1 cloud cover blocks EO collection. The commander wants confirmation of presence and any change in posture.

studentTasks.prompt: Best follow-on GEOINT product given the weather and need:
List one thing this single EO image CAN show and one thing it CANNOT show.

title: The Emitters Wake Up
objective: Differentiate ELINT/COMINT, apply LOS reasoning, and place radar activity in the kill chain.
storyText: ELINT reporting shows increasing Donovian radar emissions near the border. Activity matches a target acquisition role; fire-control activity remains unconfirmed. The Greater Caucasus ridge likely masks some coverage south of the divide.

studentTasks.prompt: Reporting on radar emissions is best categorized as:
Order the radar kill-chain steps from first to last:
Why is the absence of fire-control radar activity meaningful for engagement imminence? (1–2 sentences)

title: Night Signatures
objective: Tie an IR signature to an appropriate countermeasure choice.
storyText: A FLIR overflight detects warm vehicle signatures along two unimproved tracks near Zabzimek. Gorgan rotary-wing resupply runs the same corridor and is in suspected IR-guided MANPADS range.

studentTasks.prompt: Most appropriate aircraft countermeasure against an IR-guided MANPADS:
Briefly explain why this countermeasure (not the others) fits the threat type.

title: The Space Gap
objective: Match orbit regime to mission, classify counterspace activity, and state a collection gap.
storyText: Planners must allocate scarce space ISR. LEO offers resolution but limited revisit; GEO supports SATCOM and weather. GNSS interference is reported within ~80 km of the border.

studentTasks.prompt: Best orbit choice for high-resolution imagery of the motor pool:
GNSS jamming is best categorized as:
State one named collection gap you would surface to the commander.

title: Commander Update — Final Assessment
objective: Synthesize multi-domain reporting and answer the PIR.
storyText: The commander asks for your assessment: will Donovia conduct a limited cross-border operation into Gorgas within the next 72 hours? Provide BLUF, most likely COA, most dangerous COA, key indicators, collection gaps, recommended collection, and confidence.
